question: What is the main goal of natural family planning methods?

options.B: Identifying the fertile window to time intercourse
options.D: Permanently stopping the release of eggs

explanation: These methods focus on recognizing when ovulation happens so a couple can either avoid or achieve pregnancy. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why do many patients in primary health care clinics choose natural family planning?

options.A: They completely eliminate the risk of unintended pregnancy
options.B: They involve no financial cost or synthetic hormones
options.C: They guarantee complete protection against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: They require no daily tracking or physical observations

explanation: Natural methods appeal to many patients because they do not cost money and avoid chemical side effects. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which hormone surge directly triggers ovulation?
explanation: A sharp spike in luteinizing hormone causes the dominant ovarian follicle to rupture and release the egg. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h2)

question: How many days can healthy sperm typically survive inside the female reproductive tract?
explanation: Sperm can wait in the reproductive tract for several days, meaning intercourse before ovulation can still lead to fertilization. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h2)

question: For which client is the Standard Days Method most appropriate?

options.A: Women with completely irregular monthly bleeding
options.B: Clients who are exclusively breastfeeding an infant
options.C: Young girls who experienced their first period last month
options.D: Women with regular cycles between 26 and 32 days

explanation: The Standard Days Method relies on predictable cycle lengths falling strictly within that specific range. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h3)

question: A client has highly irregular cycles ranging from 22 to 42 days. What is the best action regarding the calendar method?

options.A: Assure her that cycle irregularity makes tracking easier
options.B: Tell her to subtract 18 from 42 to find her fertile day
options.C: Advise her that calendar calculations will be unreliable
options.D: Recommend using the Standard Days bead necklace

explanation: Wide variations in cycle length make mathematical prediction methods inaccurate and unsafe for avoiding pregnancy. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h3)

question: What does cervical mucus look and feel like at its peak fertility?

options.A: Clear, stretchy, and slippery like raw egg white
options.B: Thick, opaque, and tacky like paste
options.D: Dry, crumbly, and dark brown in color

explanation: High estrogen levels make the mucus stretchy and clear to help sperm swim easily toward the egg. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why does cervical mucus change its consistency across the menstrual cycle?

options.A: Vaginal pH drops sharply during the menstrual bleeding phase
options.B: Shifting hormone levels alter the fluid secreted by the cervix
options.C: Bacterial flora in the vagina multiply rapidly after ovulation
options.D: Dietary changes directly modify reproductive tract secretions

explanation: Estrogen and progesterone control the type of mucus the cervix produces at different times of the cycle. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h4)

question: When must a client take her basal body temperature for accuracy?

options.A: In the afternoon after eating a heavy meal
options.B: Every evening right before going to sleep
options.C: Immediately upon waking before getting out of bed
options.D: Right after finishing strenuous physical exercise

explanation: Resting body temperature must be measured before any movement or daily activities alter metabolic heat production. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h5)

question: What causes the body temperature to rise during the second half of the cycle?

options.A: Increased metabolic rate caused by fertilization
options.B: A sudden drop in circulating estrogen levels
options.C: Thickening of the uterine lining wall
options.D: Progesterone production from the corpus luteum

explanation: Progesterone is a hormone that raises the core body temperature slightly after ovulation occurs. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h5)

question: What makes the symptothermal method more reliable than calendar tracking alone?

options.A: It cross-references multiple physical signs of ovulation
options.B: It requires daily medication to suppress fertility
options.C: It relies entirely on mathematical formulas
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for daily record keeping

explanation: Using temperature, mucus, and physical symptoms together provides backup indicators if one sign is ambiguous. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a secondary sign sometimes included in symptothermal charting?

options.D: Softening or opening of the cervix

explanation: Menstrual bleeding marks the start of a new cycle, whereas secondary ovulation signs occur around the middle of the cycle. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which condition is NOT a required rule for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method to work?

options.A: The infant must be sleeping through the night without feeds
options.B: The infant must be under six months of age
options.C: The mother must practice exclusive or near-exclusive breastfeeding
options.D: The mother must not have experienced a return of menses

explanation: Night feeds are actually essential for maintaining the high hormone levels required to suppress ovulation during LAM. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h7)

question: How does frequent suckling at the breast prevent pregnancy during the postpartum period?

options.A: It causes the uterine lining to shed continuously
options.B: It permanently damages immature ovarian follicles
options.C: It thickens the cervical mucus to trap all bacteria
options.D: It suppresses hormones that stimulate the release of eggs

explanation: Nipple stimulation blocks the brain signals that trigger ovulation, keeping the woman naturally infertile temporarily. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why is partner cooperation especially important when counseling couples on natural family planning?

options.A: Husbands must calculate the basal body temperatures daily
options.B: Couples must purchase expensive electronic testing kits together
options.C: Men must physically examine the cervical mucus changes
options.D: Periods of sexual abstinence require agreement from both partners

explanation: Because natural methods rely on avoiding intercourse during fertile days, both partners must be fully committed and cooperative. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h8)

question: A newly married client wants to use a natural method, but her husband works away and her schedule causes her stress. What is the best midwifery approach?

options.A: Refuse to provide any family planning advice until her husband returns
options.B: Insist she use the calendar method regardless of her stress levels
options.C: Discuss how stress impacts cycles and explore if alternative methods suit her better
options.D: Tell her that stress has zero effect on reproductive hormone cycles

explanation: Midwives must tailor counseling to real-life situations, noting that stress and irregular routines can disrupt cycles and undermine method reliability. [learn more](BMP126_U2_T6#BMP126_U2_T6_h8)
